title: The internet is under the sea
hook: Almost all intercontinental data travels through cables on the seabed.
notes: Around 600 cables are active or planned (TeleGeography). Routes here are schematic and a small sample. Cable faults: about 150–200 per year, mostly from fishing and anchors (International Cable Protection Committee).

scenes.title: Not satellites, cables
scenes.text: Your video call to New York almost certainly runs through a cable about the width of a garden hose, lying on the ocean floor.

scenes.title: Big tech builds its own
scenes.text: Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon now pay for many new cables themselves. MAREA, Dunant and Grace Hopper cross the Atlantic; JUPITER crosses the Pacific.

scenes.title: Wrapping a continent
scenes.text: 2Africa, led by Meta with partners, circles the African continent and is one of the longest cables ever built, around 45,000 km.

scenes.title: When cables break
scenes.text: In early 2024, a ship's dragging anchor in the Red Sea cut three major cables at once. Repairs need specialised ships, and there are only a few dozen in the world.
